extracted.intended_audience: Authors of Cochrane Overviews of Reviews (overview authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Methodological and reporting guidance for preparing, conducting, analysing, and reporting Cochrane Overviews of Reviews (syntheses of systematic reviews), including decisions about inclusion, searching, overlap, data extraction, risk of bias, analysis, presentation, GRADE, and updating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion decision options for Overviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential inclusion decisions are to: include only Cochrane reviews of interventions; include all Cochrane and non-Cochrane systematic reviews (and avoid double-counting outcome data); include all Cochrane and non-Cochrane systematic reviews (regardless of double-counting outcome data); include all non-overlapping systematic reviews, and for groups of overlapping reviews include the Cochrane, most recent, highest quality, “most relevant”, or “most comprehensive” systematic review (to avoid double-counting outcome data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should choose among these options based on comprehensiveness, logistical capacity, and methodological considerations; they may also use quality/risk of bias assessments as exclusion criteria before applying these inclusion decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of double-counting primary study outcome data
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should avoid double-counting outcome data from overlapping primary studies by ensuring that each primary study’s outcome data are extracted from overlapping reviews only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is time-intensive and methodologically complex; if authors are unable to avoid double-counting for methodological or logistical reasons they may still include all reviews but must provide methodological justification, assess and document the extent of primary study overlap, and discuss limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritization criteria for overlapping reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: When avoiding overlap by selecting among overlapping reviews, authors may select the Cochrane, most recent, highest quality, 'most relevant', or 'most comprehensive' systematic review for groups of overlapping reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should operationalize the criteria used to define 'most recent', 'highest quality', 'most relevant' or 'most comprehensive' a priori where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive and reproducible literature searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a protocol is developed, conduct a literature search that is comprehensive and reproducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overviews that only include Cochrane reviews will need only to search the CDSR; if non-Cochrane reviews are included, search MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, regional and subject-specific databases (e.g. LILACS, CINAHL, PsycINFO) and systematic review repositories (e.g. Epistemonikos, KSR Evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict searches to capture systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempt to restrict searches to capture systematic reviews while minimizing capture of non-systematic review publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use search terms and MeSH headings specific to the systematic review study design (e.g. 'systematic review', 'meta-analysis') and use validated systematic review search filters; a list of validated filters is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of retrieved documents against eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document retrieved by the literature search must be assessed to see whether it meets the eligibility criteria of the Overview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the key steps in Chapter 4 Section 4.6 for inclusion processes; documents may already have been preselected during earlier decision points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Cochrane protocols and out-of-date Cochrane reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CDSR search retrieves Protocols or reviews that are not sufficiently up-to-date, Overview authors should contact Cochrane Community Support and/or review author teams to ask whether reviews are close to completion or being updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any outstanding Protocols in the reference list under 'Characteristics of reviews awaiting assessment' and consider obtaining pre-publication versions for inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to pre-specified definition of 'systematic review' for non-Cochrane SRs
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing non-Cochrane systematic reviews for inclusion, Overview authors must adhere to their pre-specified definition of a 'systematic review'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define what constitutes a systematic review in the protocol and apply consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing primary studies within broader systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Overview’s scope is narrower than the scope of an included systematic review, only the subset of primary studies within that review that fulfil the Overview’s inclusion criteria should be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess primary studies, as reported within included systematic reviews, against the Overview’s inclusion criteria (example: include only child studies when review contains adults and children).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of supplemental primary-study searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Overviews should not conduct study-level searches or new systematic reviews within an Overview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If important gaps remain after identifying eligible systematic reviews, authors may consider supplemental searches for primary studies but should re-consider whether the Overview format is appropriate because incorporating primary studies increases complexity and there is no established guidance on doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping primary study overlap (citation matrix and measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Map which primary studies are included in which systematic reviews, using citation matrices and narrative description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a citation matrix (template provided), narratively describe number/size of overlapping primary studies and the weight they contribute to analyses, and consider calculating the 'corrected covered area' to quantify overlap; assess overlap separately for each intervention comparison where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report extent and nature of primary study overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on the extent and nature of the primary study overlap should be clearly reported in the published Overview, especially if unable to avoid double-counting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how overlap could affect results and provide details on which studies overlap and how they were handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of non-identical references for the same primary study
rubrics_metrics.description: Overlapping primary studies may not be easily identifiable across systematic reviews if different references are cited to describe the same primary study (e.g. different subgroups, comparisons, outcomes, time points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully check citations and study details to identify potentially the same primary study cited differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of data to extract from included systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract data to inform risk of bias assessment of systematic reviews (and their included primary studies); descriptive characteristics of systematic reviews (and their included primary studies); quantitative outcome data; and certainty of evidence for important outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use piloted forms and ensure data extraction is planned for these categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent duplicate data extraction and piloted forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological quality/risk of bias assessments and data extraction should be conducted independently by two reviewers, with a process for resolving discrepancies, using piloted forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is highly desirable to enhance rigour and reproducibility (see Chapter 5 Section 5.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for missing, inadequately reported, or inconsistently reported data
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview authors should consider in advance how they will proceed if data are missing from, inadequately reported in, or reported differently across included systematic reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include noting gaps in coverage in the Overview, extracting missing data directly from primary studies (which may require extra resources), or re-considering the appropriateness of the Overview format if extracting substantial primary-study data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess methodological quality / risk of bias of included systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview authors can use one of three tools to assess methodological quality or risk of bias of included systematic reviews: AMSTAR, AMSTAR 2, or ROBIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a table showing how each systematic review was rated on each question of the chosen tool, the rationale behind assessments, and an overall rating where appropriate; use results to contextualize the Overview’s evidence base.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMSTAR 2 critical domains and overall confidence rating
rubrics_metrics.description: AMSTAR2 includes critical domains: protocol registered before start of review; adequacy of literature search; justification for excluded studies; risk of bias for included studies; appropriateness of meta-analytic methods; consideration of risk of bias when interpreting results; and assessing presence and likely impact of publication bias. The tool provides guidance to rate overall confidence in a review's results (high, moderate, low or critically low).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to AMSTAR2 detailed guidance when using this tool; AMSTAR2 may be preferred for reviews including randomized and non-randomized studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ROBIS for assessing risk of bias in systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: ROBIS involves three phases: 1) assessing relevance (optional); 2) identifying concerns with the systematic review process across four domains (study eligibility criteria; identification and selection of studies; data collection and study appraisal; synthesis and findings); and 3) judging overall risk of bias (low, high, unclear).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools, data extraction forms, and presentation tables are available on the ROBIS website.

rubrics_metrics.name: No single risk-of-bias tool universally recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: We cannot currently recommend one tool over another due to a lack of empirical evidence on this topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regardless of tool choice, include detailed breakdowns and rationale for ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and present risk of bias assessments for primary studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract and report the domain-specific and/or overall quality/risk of bias assessments for relevant primary studies contained within each included systematic review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally extract the assessments presented in each included review rather than repeating/updating them; present in narrative and/or tabular summaries. If reviews used different tools, extract disparate assessments as best as possible or supplement by extracting from primary studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive characteristics to extract (Box V.4.a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract basic information about systematic reviews (title, authors, year, date last up-to-date, number of studies/participants), basic info about primary studies (authors, year, design, country), systematic review search strategies, populations, interventions, comparators, primary/secondary outcomes, and additional information (Overview author comments, limitations, methodological quality/risk of bias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report these in a 'Characteristics of included reviews' table and note discrepancies between outcomes included in SRs and those pre-specified in the Overview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two main approaches to analysing outcome data: summarizing vs re-analysing
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarizing outcome data: present data in the Overview exactly as presented in included SRs (narrative or meta-analysed); Re-analysing outcome data: extract outcome data and analyse them differently (e.g. meta-analysis) than the original SRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice depends on Overview purpose, topic, and SR characteristics; both approaches lie on a continuum and may be used; re-analysis may encounter more issues with non-Cochrane SRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for summarizing outcome data
rubrics_metrics.description: When summarizing outcome data, data should be extracted as they were reported in the underlying systematic reviews and then reformatted and presented in text, tables and/or figures as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract effect estimates, 95% CIs, and measures of heterogeneity; rely on analyses reported in included SRs as much as possible; limit re-analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for re-analysing outcome data
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview authors may re-analyse outcome data to answer a different clinical question, apply consistent analyses across SRs, present results using consistent summary measures or models, or to meta-analyse data not previously pooled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard meta-analytic principles (see Chapter 10), present re-analysed outcomes in a standardized way (fixed/random effects, consistent effect measures), understand reasons behind original SR analytic choices, and guard against inappropriate informal indirect comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of outcome data and framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome data can be presented narratively and in results tables; authors could present each outcome across SRs, present results from each SR in turn, group similar SRs/outcomes together, or organize results into categories (e.g. 'clinically important' vs 'not clinically important').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid categorizing results by statistical significance only; frameworks used to present outcome data should be specified a priori or indicated as post hoc; provide references and examples where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of findings tables and cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating 'Summary of findings' tables, follow Chapter 14 layout/terminology and include references indicating which outcome data come from which SRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution against selectively reporting only statistically significant outcomes; be careful when juxtaposing data from different SRs in a single table or figure as this may invite informal indirect comparisons—only do so if avoid 'comparing' across SRs, interpret appropriately, and describe caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of GRADE to assess certainty of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Cochrane Overviews should use the GRADE tool to assess and report the certainty of evidence for each pre-defined, clinically important outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract and report GRADE assessments presented in included SRs where possible; if SRs lack GRADE assessments or if re-analysed data make SR GRADE assessments irrelevant, Overview authors may need to conduct GRADE assessments themselves using information reported in SRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and reporting requirements specific to Cochrane Overviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles should contain the phrase 'an Overview of Reviews'; titles should state whether Cochrane reviews of interventions and/or non-Cochrane systematic reviews are included; section headings should refer to 'reviews' rather than 'studies'; and there should be separate subheadings discussing methodological quality of included systematic reviews and that of their underlying primary studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the protocol and overview section templates provided (Box V.5.a and Box V.5.b) for required headers and content (e.g. criteria for selecting reviews, types of reviews/participants/interventions/outcomes, search methods, data collection and analysis, quality of included reviews, risk of bias of primary studies, summary of findings, implications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular updating of Cochrane Overviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular updating of Cochrane Overviews is very important and follows the same process as updating Cochrane reviews of interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In many cases only minor changes will be required; follow Chapter IV procedures for updating.
